prompt_bytes_frozen_statement: The panel prompt bytes are final: H11 LANDS_CLEAN; H12–H15 closed at the re-attack; H16 and H17 closed on disk under T-P032-B0d-h16h17-2026-07-31; the lens amendment landed. No further prompt or protocol edit is scheduled before publish. This block hashes that frozen tree; every digest was recomputed from the bytes on disk at build time, none was carried forward from the previous block.
publish_gate: Any field still reading `pending` blocks B0d publish. No field in this block reads `pending`; `publish_blocking_pending_fields` is empty and `publish_ready` is true.

hash_normalization.prompts_and_tool_manifest: Fields 5, 6, 7: UTF-8 bytes, BOM stripped if present, CRLF and CR normalized to LF, Unicode NFC, SHA-256 per FIPS 180-4.
hash_normalization.parameter_manifest: Field 8: JCS (RFC 8785) canonicalization, then SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonicalized string.
hash_normalization.c2d_response_metadata_blob: JCS (RFC 8785) canonicalization of the retained blob, then SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonicalized string.
hash_normalization.jcs_key_ordering_caveat: RFC 8785 specifies UTF-16 code-unit key ordering. The serializer used here sorts by Unicode code point. Every key in every object hashed by this block is ASCII, where the two orderings are identical; the builder asserts ASCII-only keys and halts otherwise. No hashed object contains a floating-point number, so RFC 8785's number-formatting rules are not load-bearing here either.

digest_recomputation_discipline: Every digest in this block was computed twice by independent paths and both results are recorded alongside it: path 1 is a separately spawned `python3 -c` process using `hashlib.sha256`; path 2 is the `sha256sum` command-line binary at /sbin/sha256sum. A third in-process read acts as a tripwire on the temp-file plumbing. A digest that does not agree with itself across paths halts the build; it is not footnoted.

rehash_vs_previous_block.statement: Every byte-derived field was recomputed from the bytes currently on disk; nothing was carried forward on the assumption a file did not change. Per seat, per field: 'held' means the digest equals the one in the previous block (T-P032-B0d-panel-commitment-block-2026-07-31); 'changed' means the H11/H12–H15/H16–H17 and lens fix cycle moved those bytes. The previous digest is recorded alongside every field under seats.<seat>.hashed_input_evidence.<field>.previous_block_sha256.

c2d_response_metadata_blob_rule.ruling_quoted: The blob is the response envelope minus message content, which is what C2(d)'s own parenthetical enumerates (`id`, `model`, `type`, `stop_reason`, `usage`, plus any `system_fingerprint`). `choices` is the message-content carrier and is dropped. Whichever form is chosen, the ticket publishes the exact rule it applied alongside the digest, so a third party can re-derive it rather than guess.
executable_rule: 1. Take the provider's response body as returned, parsed as JSON, at the top level.

2. RETAIN every top-level key EXCEPT the message-content carrier `choices`. The retained key set is whatever the provider's envelope actually carries; it is not a fixed list. Observed key sets: on the OpenAI chat-completions envelope for A1 the retained top-level keys are exactly `created`, `id`, `model`, `object`, `service_tier`, `system_fingerprint`, `usage`; on the DeepSeek chat-completions envelope for A2 they are exactly `created`, `id`, `model`, `object`, `system_fingerprint`, `usage` (DeepSeek returns no `service_tier` key).
3. DROP the key `choices` IN FULL — the entire array, not only its message-content leaves. `choices` is the message-content carrier.
4. Retain a key whose value is `null` AS a present key with a null value. Do not drop null-valued keys. `system_fingerprint` on the A1 envelope is exactly that case.
5. Do not coerce, reorder, round, or re-type any retained value. Values are byte-equivalent to what the provider returned.
7. SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonicalized string. That digest is the C2(d) commitment.
c2d_response_metadata_blob_rule.which_form_is_committed: The SECONDARY form from each probe (section 4b of the probe markdown), with `choices` dropped entirely, IS the C2(d) commitment. It is the redaction-independent form, so the digest encodes nobody's judgment call about what counts as message content.
c2d_response_metadata_blob_rule.known_and_accepted_cost: Dropping `choices` in full removes `finish_reason` from the committed surface. That is a known and accepted cost of the ruling, not an oversight.
c2d_response_metadata_blob_rule.alternate_reading_status: The PRIMARY form from each probe (section 4a, `choices` retained with assistant message content keys omitted) is the non-committed alternate reading. It is recorded per seat, not deleted, so the record shows what was considered and rejected.

provider_shape_transfer.statement: The rule transfers to the DeepSeek envelope with one top-level key-set difference, stated here so the rule stays executable by a stranger against each provider's actual envelope rather than silently generalised.
provider_shape_transfer.difference: DeepSeek's envelope carries no `service_tier` key; every other retained key is common to both. DeepSeek's `system_fingerprint` is a non-null string where OpenAI's came back as a present key with a `null` value. DeepSeek's `usage` object additionally carries `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` and `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`, which are retained as returned per step 2 — the rule retains whatever the envelope carries outside `choices`.

c2d_response_metadata_blob_rule.why_the_rule_is_published: A digest without its rule is an unverifiable number. This rule is stated so a third party can re-derive the digest rather than guess at it.

byte_discipline_observations.observation: The three panel tool-availability manifests are the 2-byte literal `[]` with NO trailing newline. The B1 emitter's tool-availability manifest was the 3-byte `[]\n`. The panel field-7 digest (identical across all three seats; see seats.<seat>.fields.7_tool_availability.sha256) therefore differs from the B1 emitter block's 37517e5f3dc66819f61f5a7bb8ace1921282415f10551d2defa5c3eb0985b570 for the trailing-newline reason alone.
byte_discipline_observations.assessment: Not a defect. C2(c) says the committed manifest is the literal string `[]` and the committed hash is the SHA-256 of that literal string; the panel files are that literal string exactly. Recorded so no reader mistakes the digest difference for a content difference.
